 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Indiana Fever player Kelsey Mitchell posted an emotional message on Instagram to express herself. After a season in which she was one of the best players in the league, Mitchell still ended up on the receiving end of criticism. 
 She averaged 24.7 points on an efficient 50.9% shooting from the field and 45% from the three-point range. Mitchell's brilliance helped her make it to the All-Star Game and the First-Team All-WNBA.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement With her on the team, Caitlin Clark received great support, as she had a player who could ease the scoring burden on her. Despite playing elite basketball, Mitchell was often criticised by fans, and she made sure to make it clear in her exit interview after the Fever's first-round exit against the Las Vegas Aces.
 Caitlin Clark and Aliyah Boston comment on Kelsey Mitchell's emotional post
 Mitchell revealed that playing alongside Clark meant that there was a lot of scrutiny. Moreover, Clark's star power led to a lot of Mitchell's work being overlooked.
 Although she has a great relationship with CC, Mitchell's comments were directed at the fans, who made it a point to make it difficult for her teammates.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "Imagine no one believing, fr…. while fightin (fighting) to keep believin (believing) in yourself. Nun (Nothing) colder, but wise than that. Did what I can, always lent my hand and then imagine being wrong in they eyes no matter what… Played the game how the game goes… zero is zero no matter what direction it goes," Mitchell wrote in the caption of an image carousel from the season.
 The post had images of everyone on the Fever team. Clark commented with a heart emoji, and Aliyah Boston said: "Zero is always gonna be zero, my gurlllllll."
 The post comes days after the player unfollowed the Fever on her Instagram, sparking rumours of a potential exit. She is an unrestricted free agent this offseason, and with all that happened during the exit interview, the veteran could possibly be on her way out of Indiana.
 Mitchell revealed that she would be 'selfish' in her decision when asked about her future during the exit interview. Washington Mystics are a team that has been linked to her, but nothing has been confirmed yet, as the Fever could still make a push to get her back to the team.
